title: Rejoice not (Avot 4:19, Proverbs 24:17)
hookLine: a group chat laughing at someone's fall: Shmuel the Small taught "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth"
tomorrow: learning young or learning old: which one actually sticks?

lines: SHE'S THE ONE WHO BEAT YOU.
cards: The clip is already going around. Someone's big moment went wrong, and the group chat is doing what group chats do: the replays, the jokes, the crying-laughing faces. And she isn't even a friend.
She's the one who beat you. Do you laugh too? A sage called Shmuel the Small answered with a single verse, and it's the whole of his saying in Avot.

teach.h: HIS WHOLE SAYING IS A VERSE.
teach.b: Shmuel the Small doesn't write anything new.

teach.h: REJOICE NOT WHEN THINE ENEMY FALLETH.
teach.b: His entire teaching in Avot is a quotation from Proverbs: "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth." And don't let your heart be glad when he stumbles.
The next verse gives a reason: lest the Lord see it, and it displease him.
That's one to tell a friend tonight: a sage whose whole saying is somebody else's verse, and it asks a lot. Not a friend. An enemy.
Not a stranger's fall. A rival's. Rejoice not.
Now the week, because it's all here. Not in our hands: you can't explain why she got the slot. Greet first: say hi anyway.
The corridor: get ready where no one sees. One hour here: use it to make something right. And timing is kindness: wait for the moment.
Put them together and Shmuel's verse is what's left.

how: At the Passover seder many Jews spill a drop of wine for each of the ten plagues, a custom often explained as lessening joy over the suffering of others, even of enemies.

o: don't celebrate when an enemy falls, even in your heart
don't cheer too loudly when your own team wins
don't celebrate a holiday while you're in mourning

games.q: the verse and the week — tap the pairs.
p: his whole saying is a verse
lest the Lord see it and be displeased

s: the verse is only about not mocking your friends
it's about your enemy: rejoice not when thine enemy falleth.
Shmuel the Small's saying in Avot is a quotation from Proverbs
his entire teaching there is the verse.
it's fine to enjoy a rival's fall as long as you didn't cause it
the verse says don't let your heart be glad even when he stumbles.

games.q: the coworker who took credit for your work gives a presentation that goes badly, and the team chat lights up with jokes. what fits Shmuel the Small's verse?
o: stay out of the jokes, and don't let your heart cheer either.
add one joke; after what he did, a little laughter is only fair.
laugh privately but stay quiet in the chat, so no one sees it.
games.why: rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and don't let your heart be glad. the verse reaches past the chat, into the heart.

practice: With a pen, write the first name of someone whose stumble you'd be tempted to enjoy. Under it, write one ordinary thing you hope goes right for them this week. Leave the page face down, and rest for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Rejoice not. Shmuel the Small's saying, the verse from Proverbs: rejoice not when your enemy falls.

orig.note: Hebrew, Proverbs 24:17: when your enemy falls, do not rejoice.

carryVoice: Pocket this: rejoice not, even when it's the one who beat you. Two weeks of chapter four, forty-three of sixty.
